newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends flat ahead of CPI, seen lower.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends flat ahead of CPI, seen lower.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed flat on Monday as the market awaited key Consumer Price Index data on Tuesday with the expectation of a lower currency. "I think people are a little bit negative on the Kiwi generally going into the CPI," said a chief bank dealer.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6932/39 and at 68.75 on its Trade-Weighted Index, almost unchanged from its 0.6934/41 and 68.75 open.
Dealers said early buying ran out of steam with the Australian dollar struggling over most of the session and dollar/yen staying well supported.
But trade was muted, with most already positioned for a March quarter CPI number below Reserve Bank forecasts.
"Tomorrow is pivotal with the CPI, and we're all waiting to see what happens there, and where that leaves the Reserve Bank in terms of monetary policy," the chief dealer said.
"I think the market is pretty much positioned looking for a lower currency, probably more on a TWI basis than Kiwi/U.S.."
The Reserve Bank has forecast core inflation at 0.5 percent in the March quarter, while economists polled by Reuters on average expect 0.41 percent.
Some analysts predict that if the market does not ease conditions sufficiently on the back of a benign CPI number, the Reserve Bank may comment that monetary conditions are tighter than necessary.
Dealers said the CPI would have to come in significantly below the Reserve Bank's forecast for the Kiwi to come off very far.
They expect the currency to trade a 0.6920-45 range overnight.
